args.query: replication slot inactive retaining WAL disk full no space left

events.statement: payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% (13:00-14:50) to ~61% at the 15:00 bucket and stayed elevated (~61-64%) through 16:50.

First payment-service error is 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' at 15:00:26; this same pattern accounts for all 354 errors in the window (first_match 15:00:26).
ledger-db logs show PANIC/could-not-extend-file 'No space left on device' errors starting 15:01:01 and continuing to the end of data (16:57:21).
ledger-db disk_used_pct rose monotonically from 84.03% at 12:00 to 100.0% by the 15:02 bucket, and remained 100% through 16:59.
ledger-db warned 'replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 33916 MB of WAL' at 14:34:05, growing to 77371 MB by 14:49:47 — before the 14:46 deploy.
The only deployment in the window is payment-service dep-6203 v6.0.0 'New UPI mandate flow' at 14:46:00, rolled back at 15:12:00; there were no config/feature-flag changes.
payment-service errors continued AFTER the 15:12 rollback: 295 further errors between 15:20:03 and 16:57:54, all 'No space left on device'.
order-service, which also uses ledger-db but was not part of the v6.0.0 deploy, shows the identical failure: 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device' starting 15:00:42 through 16:57:47.
ledger-db is a shared Postgres used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service (dependency graph).
bank-partner-api error rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout (13:00-16:45), so the external dependency was healthy.
A prior incident HIST-114 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL' (2025-04-18) had the same root cause: inactive replication slot retaining WAL until disk filled.
Interpretation: payment-service errors are a downstream symptom of the ledger-db disk-exhaustion; the v6.0.0 deploy is temporally coincidental, not causal.
